title: Extensible tool-call schema DSL: coercion rules, compatibility layer, and user-facing error taxonomy
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: Our current function/tool calling validation uses a strict JSON Schema pass/fail model which causes a lot of user-facing errors when clients send legacy payload shapes, slightly-mismatched types (numbers as strings), or include optional aliased keys. That leads to high friction and support volume. Goal: design an extensible, opt-in schema DSL for tool parameters which: (1) expresses coercion rules (e.g., coerce string->int when safe), (2) declares compatibility aliases and deprecations, (3) controls unknown-field policies (error/warn/ignore), and (4) produces a stable, actionable error taxonomy surface to SDKs and Console for better debugging.
acceptance_criteria: DSL spec doc published in Confluence with examples for coercion, aliasing, and unknown-field policy
Runtime validator implemented behind a feature flag for hosted API that supports: strict, lenient, and hybrid modes
SDKs receive structured error codes and human-readable messages for the new taxonomy (INVALID_PARAM, MISSING_REQUIRED, COERCION_APPLIED, DEPRECATED_ALIAS_USED, UNKNOWN_FIELD_WARNING)
Compatibility layer supports schema version header and automatic alias mapping for v1->v2 of a sample tool (search.indexDocument)
E2E tests covering edge cases: ambiguous enum strings, numeric overflow on coercion, array element coercion, and partial validation with warnings
decisions: Adopt a small DSL layered on top of JSON Schema instead of inventing a wholly new language to reuse existing validators
Coercion is opt-in per-field using 'coerce' directives (values: 'none','safe','aggressive'); default is 'none'
Unknown-field policy is configurable at tool-level: 'error' | 'warn' | 'ignore'. Console will surface warnings in a new 'Parameter Warnings' section
Error taxonomy will use stable error codes and include 'hints' metadata string that SDKs can display — but runtime payloads will not include executable objects (hints are strings)
Backcompat: map deprecated aliases in the compatibility layer before validation; emit DEPRECATED_ALIAS_USED warnings but do not fail requests
implementation_notes: Spec: extend JSON Schema with a top-level 'x-redwood' object per property with fields: coerce, aliases, deprecated, unknownPolicy (tool-level)
Runtime: validator pipeline stages: pre-coercion alias-mapping -> type/coercion rules -> schema validation -> post-validation warnings -> normalized payload to handler
Coercion rules: 'safe' allows string->number when string is numeric and within range; 'aggressive' also allows 'true'/'false' strings to booleans and lenient ISO8601 parsing to date-time
Partial validation: when unknownPolicy='warn' continue with best-effort and attach UNKNOWN_FIELD_WARNING code; when 'error' return INVALID_PARAM with list of fields

SDK contract: errors returned as JSON with keys 'code' (enum), 'message' (string), 'fields' (list of strings) and optional 'hint' (string). Example code names: INVALID_PARAM, MISSING_REQUIRED, COERCION_APPLIED, DEPRECATED_ALIAS_USED, UNKNOWN_FIELD_WARNING
Compatibility shim: support 'X-Redwood-Schema-Version' header to choose alias and coercion policies; default to latest but provide 'legacy' compatibility mapping for common older clients
Telemetry: log events for COERCION_APPLIED and DEPRECATED_ALIAS_USED with anonymized hashes of tool names and field names for monitoring; surface rates in Console
Rollout: feature flag per-customer. Start with internal dogfood workspace in hosted API, then opt-in beta customers, then global default after 6 weeks of signals
